title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 6
paragraphs: So they remained in Euboea and fought a sea-battle, which came about as follows. When the barbarians had arrived at Aphetai about the beginning of the afternoon, having been told even before arriving that a few Greek ships were stationed at Artemisium, and now seeing them for themselves, they were eager to attack, to see if they could capture them. They thought it not yet good to sail directly against them, for this reason: for fear that the Greeks, when they saw them coming, would set out in flight and darkness would catch them as they fled — in which case, they reckoned, the Greeks would likely escape; whereas, by their calculation, not even the fire-bearer should get away and save his life.
